steps.name: Library size and count QC across all 12 samples
steps.question: What are the raw and normalized library sizes (total counts) for each of the 12 samples (sample_01 through sample_12, 6 AD lesional vs 6 control), and how does sample_01 compare quantitatively to the cohort median and to the other 11 samples?
acceptance_criteria: Table reporting total raw counts per sample for all 12 samples, sorted ascending
Median library size computed and each sample's ratio to median reported
Explicit quantification of sample_01's library size relative to the median (confirm or refute the ~4x-below-median claim from the data profile)
Number of genes with zero counts or near-zero detection reported per sample to flag any additional shallow samples
Bar plot of library sizes annotated by condition (AD lesional vs control) and saved as a figure

steps.name: Variance-stabilized normalization and PCA of all 12 samples
steps.question: After variance-stabilizing transformation (DESeq2 VST or rlog) of the 12000 x 12 raw count matrix, how do the 12 samples separate in PCA space, does the AD lesional vs control grouping emerge on the top components, and does sample_01 appear as an outlier along any principal component?
acceptance_criteria: Raw counts loaded from counts.csv and matched to metadata.csv condition labels for all 12 samples
VST or rlog applied via DESeq2 on the full 12-sample count matrix
PCA computed on the transformed data; PC1 vs PC2 (and PC2 vs PC3) scatter plots produced, colored by condition and labeled by sample ID
Percent variance explained reported for at least the first 4 PCs
Explicit statement of where sample_01 falls relative to the other 11 samples on each of the top PCs, with a numeric outlier assessment (e.g., distance from group centroid or z-score of PC loading)

steps.name: Sample-to-sample distance matrix and hierarchical clustering
steps.question: Using the VST-transformed 12-sample expression matrix, what do pairwise sample-to-sample Euclidean distances and hierarchical clustering reveal about sample grouping by condition (AD lesional vs control), and does sample_01 cluster as an outlier or fall within its expected condition group?
acceptance_criteria: Pairwise sample-to-sample distance matrix computed on the same VST-transformed data used for PCA in T1S2, for all 12 samples
Heatmap of the 12x12 distance matrix produced with hierarchical clustering dendrogram and condition annotation bar
Sample_01's distances to every other sample reported explicitly, contrasted against the median inter-sample distance for the cohort
Statement on whether sample_01 clusters with its labeled condition group or forms a singleton/outlier branch

steps.name: Verdict on sample_01: retain, downweight, or exclude
steps.question: Given sample_01's library size (~4x below median per the data profile), its position in PCA space, and its sample-to-sample distances relative to the other 11 samples, what is the recommended disposition for sample_01 before differential expression testing — keep as-is, keep with a flag/sensitivity analysis, or exclude?
acceptance_criteria: Synthesizes numeric evidence from T1S1 (library size ratio), T1S2 (PCA outlier position), and T1S3 (distance-matrix outlier position) into a single written verdict

Explicitly states whether sample_01's low depth is likely to bias downstream DE results (e.g., via gene dropout, increased dispersion, or shrinkage toward zero) given it is n=6 per group with only 12 total samples

Gives a concrete recommendation: retain and proceed, retain but flag/run DE with and without sample_01 as a sensitivity check, or exclude and lose statistical power (explicitly note the power cost of dropping to 5 vs 6 in a small design)
Does not claim differential expression was tested — this step precedes and does not substitute for a DE analysis

plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin RNA-seq QC
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a pre-testing QC pass on the 12-sample (6 AD lesional vs 6 control) skin bulk RNA-seq count matrix (12000 genes x 12 samples, raw Salmon gene-level counts). The data context already flags sample_01 as having a library size ~4x below the median, a known caveat for this cohort. Before any differential expression is run, we need: (1) library size accounting across all 12 samples, (2) a variance-stabilized PCA to see whether sample_01 or any other sample separates as an outlier and whether condition drives the dominant axes, (3) a sample-to-sample distance/clustering view to corroborate the PCA read, and (4) an explicit verdict step that synthesizes the library-size, PCA, and distance evidence into a decision on sample_01 (retain, downweight, or exclude) with justification. All steps operate on the same 12x12000 counts.csv and metadata.csv, so this is a single track on the bulk-transcriptomics-agent, run as sequential/dependent steps since each downstream check consumes the normalized object from the QC step.
